basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 9.' and it opens 'Vers. 9. Recordatus est somniorum quae aliquando viderat. Quod videlicet sol et luna et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 9. Recordatus est somniorum quae aliquando viderat. Quod videlicet sol et luna et stellae illum adorarent. Et revera Christum adorat omnis creatura, et spiritaliter adorat eum sanctorum perfectio, Ecclesiae splendor, et omnis electorum multitudo, juvenes et virgines, senes cum junioribus.
